items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: You see Bernard Goldberg, a Jewish friend of mine that liked me from the first day that he met me.

ctx.x: You see Bernard Goldberg, a Jewish friend of mine that liked me from the first day that he met me. In fact this guy was driving a big black Pierce Hour in those days and he would go into me just like it was my car. So when I quit Charles Band in Dallas and I went back to New Orleans, he came down there and he told me, he said, why don't you get your band? Oh I said Mr. Goldberg, I'm a little too young for that. He said, go ahead and get your band, I'll get a job for you. In fact Bernard Goldberg had already had…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: He says, I'll give you a thousand dollars. So he gave me a thousand dollars. I got around here and got these guys together... The first job was to stay for him in Dallas.

ctx.x: What about this Bernard Goldberg? Had you get in touch with him?

Well, Bernard Goldberg was an admirer of, he admired my playing and he thought that I would make a band leader. And he would come to Shadowland and he would ask me to organize a band. So I told him I wasn't ready. And when I came back here to New Orleans in, oh, it was 1929. But, Bernard came over and he said, why don't you get a band together? He says, I get you a real good job to start off with. I said, well, that sounds all right. He says, you need any money? He says, I'll give you a thousand dollars. So he…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: made by one of the best tailors in Dallas through one of the bookers, the man that found me, Bernard Goldberg.

ctx.x: I remember seeing a picture of Duke Ellington wearing pants like that.

Well this was the style in those days. And this whole outfit was made by one of the best tailors in Dallas through one of the bookers, the man that found me, Bernard Goldberg. This other picture you see here is later on when I had stopped playing I was only featuring myself on two or three numbers. I had to take care of the business of the band. This was taken in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. And naturally this one here that you're looking at I was eight years old. This is in my backyard. You notice the wash tubs?…
That's a nice old style horn.
